question_text: What are the components of a transcription unit?

insider_note: Three components, three jobs. Promoter, structural gene, terminator — in that order, because the order is the direction of transcription.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three components
steps.margin_note: All three, numbered, in transcription order.
lines: A TRANSCRIPTION UNIT has THREE components:
steps.why: Transcription needs somewhere to start, something to copy and somewhere to stop, which is exactly these three.
common_mistakes: Naming the operator. The operator belongs to an OPERON, not to a transcription unit.
Giving two components. There are THREE.

steps.label: What each does
steps.margin_note: One line each, with the ends named. Seven lines.

lines.text: Promoter starts it, gene is copied,

lines: The PROMOTER lies at the 5' end and is where RNA
The STRUCTURAL GENE is the DNA that is actually
The TERMINATOR lies at the 3' end and defines
steps.why: The promoter and terminator fix both ends, so between them they define exactly which stretch of DNA becomes RNA.
common_mistakes: Saying the promoter is transcribed. It is a BINDING site, not part of the message.
Placing the terminator at the 5' end. It is at the 3' end.
steps.memory_tip: Promoter at the 5' end, terminator at the 3'.
